findings.title: Migration can fail on rerun or drifted databases because DROP INDEX is unconditional
findings.evidence: The upgrade path executes an unconditional index drop before any other work, so a database that is missing that index due to prior partial cleanup or schema drift will raise and abort the migration.
findings.recommendation: Use an idempotent form such as DROP INDEX IF EXISTS, or query schema metadata before dropping so the migration succeeds on databases that have already lost this index.

findings.title: Destructive table drop has no guard or visible prerequisite check
findings.evidence: The migration now unconditionally removes the entire legacy_users table. From this diff alone there is no check that data was copied elsewhere, no backup step, and no IF EXISTS guard, so running it against a database where the table still contains needed rows or is already absent will either destroy data or abort the migration.
findings.recommendation: Only drop the table after an explicit verified data migration step, and make the operation idempotent with DROP TABLE IF EXISTS or a schema existence check. If data must be preserved, archive or copy it before deletion.
